why: B moved strictly more real traffic and did the harder work to get it there — porting the n=5 review ensemble (the pipeline's largest prompt, two calls per idea) off an untranslatable parameter rather than leaving it on OpenAI or silently dropping n, and unlocking DeepSeek with a host unlock plus catalog map — while also catching that the scanner's 'routing' verdict on the Gemini line is a false positive because every Gemini id is BYOK. Its system-level judgment is the one an expert would make for this app: a per-stage token profile (50 ideas x 3 rounds, 10 novelty rounds each re-sending experiment.py, 11 review calls run twice, ~45 writeup passes), stage labels so one cache key stops colliding across stages, and block-level Claude caching measured at ~78% off the novelty loop — against A's coarser, more generic cache-key-plus-metadata set.
A_best: The resilience item: fallbacks: [gpt-4.1] plus provider_timeout on the Responses paths, correctly reasoned through the capability guard (active model, accepts temperature) and honestly caveated that a silent candidate swap is invisible in the app's logs and that a 504 is not retried by the app's backoff — the one genuine Router lever B's shown items don't cover; plus the sharp negative finding that Flex is worth nothing here since no model the repo names has a Flex tier.
B_best: Refusing to drop n in policy and instead porting the 5-way ensemble to per-response calls, with the cost delta quantified honestly (+$0.10 per ensemble on gpt-4o, roughly halved by the cache key) and a follow-up branch that parallelizes the five round trips it introduced — it moved the single most expensive prompt in the pipeline onto Router instead of filing it as a proposal.
A_worst: Its own numbers don't hold together: the summary claims '7 of 9 route' while its call table marks DeepSeek and Gemini as staying on provider, and the validation's verified list silently counts those three as routed — A never flags the false positive B caught. It also left both addressable blockers (the n=5 ensemble, the DeepSeek host) as proposals.
B_worst: It folds prompt_cache_key and metadata into the migration itself (m9) rather than keeping the move behaviour-neutral and the improvement separable, and its highest-ranked quick win (i3) is app-logic repair — the NaN/IndexError crashes and stale novelty context — with no Router leverage at all, which also quietly changes review-aggregation semantics.
